submissionRequirements.title: Title & Abstract
submissionRequirements.text: A concise title and an abstract (max 300 words).

submissionRequirements.title: Paper (PDF)
submissionRequirements.text: One anonymized PDF (max 10 MB) in the IEEE conference format; no page limit.

submissionRequirements.title: Session Track
submissionRequirements.text: Clear indication of Tutorial or Regular Paper.

submissionRequirements.title: Outline & Schedule
submissionRequirements.text: A breakdown of how the allotted time will be used.
items: Tutorials: detailed breakdown of the 5-minute morning presentation and milestone-based progression for the 90-minute workshop.
Regular papers: clear breakdown of the 10-minute presentation structure.

submissionRequirements.title: Prerequisites & Toolchain (Tutorials)
submissionRequirements.text: List of required software, target OS compatibility, hardware dependencies, and recommended skill level.

submissionRequirements.title: Workshop Size (Tutorials)
submissionRequirements.text: Choose a workshop for 25 or 50 participants. If the workshop needs equipment, prepare 10 sets for 25 participants or 20 sets for 50 participants.

submissionRequirements.title: Participant Hardware Requirements (Tutorials)
submissionRequirements.text: The minimum hardware participants' laptops must meet, such as CPU, memory (RAM), GPU, free disk space and operating system. These requirements are published to attendees.

submissionRequirements.title: Teaching Assistant (Tutorials)
submissionRequirements.text: At least one teaching assistant (TA) to help participants during the practical part of the workshop.

submissionRequirements.title: Interactive Demo Video (Tutorials only)
submissionRequirements.text: A short demonstration video (2–5 minutes) showcasing the functioning prototype, project workflow, or target outcomes participants will build during the workshop.
items: Please provide a publicly viewable or unlisted link (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, or Google Drive).
This video is crucial for the program committee to evaluate technical feasibility and participant engagement.

submissionRequirements.title: Author Bio
submissionRequirements.text: Professional background (max 150 words), previous presentation experience, and relevant project links (e.g., GitHub, Google Scholar, LinkedIn).

items.q: What can I submit to ICAAS?
items.a: Two kinds of proposals: Tutorials (6 presentation slots), which engage the audience interactively through a presentation and a workshop, and Regular Papers (10 presentation slots), which present academic work relevant to the conference theme.

items.q: What is the difference between the two tracks?
items.a: Tutorial authors give a 5-minute presentation in the morning and run a 90-minute workshop in the afternoon. Regular paper authors give a 10-minute talk in the late morning, after the tutorial presentations, and present a poster in the afternoon, during the coffee break while the workshops take place.

The paper as one PDF file (max 10 MB) in the IEEE conference format, a title and an abstract of at most 300 words, the session track, an outline and schedule, and an author bio of at most 150 words with previous presentation experience and relevant project links. Tutorials also need the prerequisites and toolchain, the workshop size, the laptop hardware requirements for participants, the teaching assistant(s) and a 2–5 minute demo video.

items.q: Which paper format should I use?
items.a: Use the IEEE conference template (Microsoft Word, US letter or A4, or LaTeX, also on Overleaf), available from IEEE through the Downloads page. There is no page limit. Submit the paper as one anonymized PDF of at most 10 MB; accepted papers are due in the same format as camera-ready papers by March 31, 2027.

Yes. Proposals undergo double-blind peer review on technical depth and originality, clarity and feasibility, the engagement plan, and alignment with current industry and academic trends. Keep names and affiliations out of the paper, title, abstract and outline.

items.q: Do I have to use the ICAAS slide template?
items.a: Yes. All authors of accepted tutorials and regular papers must prepare their slides with the official ICAAS slide template, available on the Downloads page.

items.q: How does the 40% author feedback work?
items.a: Tutorial authors receive feedback based on attendance: 40% of the registration fees of their workshop. An engaging topic that draws more participants results in more feedback.

items.q: How large is a workshop, and who provides the equipment?
items.a: Authors choose a workshop for 25 or 50 participants and prepare all equipment and environment set-ups: 10 equipment sets for 25 participants or 20 sets for 50 participants, if the workshop needs equipment. Attendees bring their own laptops.

Authors provide the laptop hardware requirements of their workshop (for example CPU, memory, GPU, disk space and operating system), and they are published on the workshop pages. Please check them before registering for a workshop.

items.q: Do I need a teaching assistant?
items.a: Yes. Each workshop should have at least one teaching assistant (TA) to help participants during the practical part.
Registration opens after the notification of acceptance. Dates are listed on the Important Dates page; subscribe to updates to be notified.

items.q: Do participants register separately for workshops?
items.a: Yes. Workshop seats are registered separately from the conference registration and are limited to the workshop size chosen by the authors.

items.q: Where and when will the conference take place?
items.a: The venue and dates will be announced on this website and in the site header.
